transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

Yes. Once the interior has been cleaned, the common causes are stagnant water/debris in the defrost drain or drip tray, or residue caught around door seals, drawer runners or underneath removable drawers. The type and location of the smell will separate those from anything more serious. 1. If it smells burning, of hot plastic, or is strongest at the plug, socket or rear of the appliance, switch it off and unplug it now. Do not continue using it; that needs an engineer/electrician check.
2. If it is musty or drain-like, switch off and unplug it, then check for standing water, slime or food debris in the bottom channels of the fridge compartment and around the drain opening, if visible. Use a cloth only—do not push wire or sharp objects into it.
3. If it is sour/rotting, remove drawers and wipe the seals and drawer channels; hidden spills are often the source even after a general clean. What does the smell resemble, and where is it strongest?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

It smells like hot plastic, a sort of electrical burning smell, and it's stronger round the back and side of the fridge than inside it. I've also noticed the plug feels a bit warm and there's an occasional buzzing from the back.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use the fridge-freezer again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer; the warm plug and electrical-burning smell make this an overheating electrical fault, not a cleaning or drain issue. The most likely areas are the plug/socket or mains lead, with the occasional rear buzz also leaving a compressor start relay or rear wiring fault as a possibility. A normal compressor hum is not a concern, but a hot-plastic smell and warm plug are not normal. With it unplugged and allowed to cool, only visually inspect the plug, socket and visible lead for scorching, melting, browning or looseness—do not dismantle anything. If there is any damage at the socket or plug, use an electrician as well as, or before, an appliance engineer. If those look normal, an appliance engineer still needs to inspect the rear electrical components and compressor-start circuit before it is powered again.

candidates: Stagnant water or debris in the defrost drain/drip tray (medium)
Residue or spoiled food in a hidden area such as a door seal or drawer channel (medium)
